app.name: Skylog
app.tagline: Look up, find it, log it, learn it.

sky.circularViewHelp: See the sky hemisphere centered on the zenith, then drag to explore.

layer.realSkyHint: Fewer stars, like your light-polluted sky. Adjust sky brightness below (1 darkest – 9 inner city).
layer.milkyWayHint: Visible at night with atmosphere on. Turn atmosphere off to see it during daytime.
layer.groundTransparencyHint: 0% is opaque; 100% reveals the sky below the horizon.

tonight.title: Tonight
tonight.darkNone: Moon up all night — no dark hours

sensor.ar: Point your phone at the sky (sensor mode)
sensor.unsupported: Motion sensors aren't available in this browser. Drag to look around. (You can try the flow with Settings › Developer › Sensor simulator.)
sensor.anomaly: Possible compass interference — move away from metal or magnets
sensor.simulatorHint: On desktop, use the alpha/beta/gamma sliders to mimic how the phone is held.

permission.deniedHelp: Motion & orientation access was denied. You can keep using the app in manual mode.
permission.deniedIosSteps: On iPhone, close and reopen the Safari tab or home-screen app, then reconnect. You can move the sky with your finger meanwhile.

geo.unsupported: This browser can't provide your location. Add an observing site manually.
geo.denied: Location access was denied. Allow it in your browser's site settings, or add a site manually.
geo.timeout: Couldn't get your location (timed out). Try again with a clear view of the sky.
geo.unavailable: Location isn't available right now. Using your saved site.

wizard.title: Star alignment
wizard.step1: Pick a bright object you can see clearly right now.
wizard.noCandidates: No bright objects are high enough right now. Use Polaris or the Moon if you can see them.
wizard.step2: Point the back of your phone at it so it sits in the crosshairs, then tap “Lined up”.
wizard.dragHint: Drag sideways to nudge azimuth, up or down to nudge altitude (0.5° steps).
wizard.done: Aligned to {{target}}. Check that other objects land near the crosshairs too.

settings.declinationHint: Corrects compass headings from magnetic to true north (WMM2025). Currently {{d}}°.
settings.keepLevelHint: Ignores phone tilt (roll) so the horizon stays level.

sites.title: Observing sites
sites.name: Name (e.g. Home balcony)
sites.rangeHint: Drag on the ring to mark the directions you can actually see from here (balcony, yard). Tonight's picks only use this range.
sites.autoLocationHint: Refresh location when opening or returning to the app. Choosing a saved site turns this off.

settings.title: Settings
settings.nightModeHint: Turns the whole app red to protect your night vision.
settings.keepAwakeHint: Stops the screen turning off while you observe.
settings.debugHudHint: Shows fps, frame time and draw calls.
settings.glassHint: Turn off for solid panels over the sky — smoother on older phones.

about.title: About & licenses
about.dataLicense: Data packs: CC BY-SA 4.0 (based on HYG and OpenNGC)

debug.title: Data packs
debug.noData: No data packs yet — run pnpm data:build.

object.bestWindowHint: Above {{alt}}° while the sky is fully dark
object.verdictNote: Rough estimate from sky brightness (Bortle {{bortle}}), the Moon and altitude. Nebulae and galaxies are judged by surface brightness, so their result is less certain.

tip.alt: Height above the horizon. 0° is the horizon, 90° is overhead.
tip.az: Direction measured clockwise from north. East 90°, south 180°, west 270°.
tip.mag: Apparent brightness. Lower numbers are brighter — each magnitude is about 2.5× brighter.
tip.twilight: The time after sunset (or before sunrise) when the sky isn't fully dark yet. It's fully dark once the Sun is 18° below the horizon (end of astronomical twilight).

weather.title: Weather
weather.summaryCloudy: Average cloud cover {{cloud}}% · no clear gap tonight
weather.dew: Dew likely from {{from}} ({{n}} h) — bring a dew heater or hood
weather.dewInWindow: Dew risk for {{dur}} of your window

recommend.title: Tonight’s picks
recommend.planHint: Tap ☆ to save to your plan
recommend.none: Nothing to recommend in this window. Try another time or gear.

phenomena.title: This month’s events
phenomena.oppositionDetail: Brightest and largest of the year · mag {{mag}} · {{au}} AU

elongationDetail.morning: Look low in the east before sunrise
elongationDetail.evening: Look low in the west after sunset

phenomena.perigeeDetail: The Moon is near its closest point and looks slightly larger
phenomena.meteorDetail: Up to {{zhr}}/h · conditions {{cond}} · Moon {{moon}}% · best around {{time}}
phenomena.brilliancyDetail: Venus at its brightest for the year · mag {{mag}}
phenomena.elongationHidden: Large elongation, but it stays low near the horizon from Korea

meteor.title: Meteor showers
meteor.noneActive: No meteor shower is active right now.

guideAuto.title: Start without aligning a star
guideAuto.intro: Sensors and the compass estimate your direction. Point the top edge of your phone toward the sky you want to explore.
guideAuto.estimateHelp: Nearby metal can affect the compass. Choose star calibration for a closer telescope alignment.
guideAuto.compassHelp: Hold your phone fairly flat and move it slowly. If no compass heading is available, use optional star calibration or the sky map.
guideAuto.live: Sky in the direction of your phone’s top edge
guideAuto.skyLabel: Night sky showing the target and surrounding stars
guideAuto.nearHelp: Compare the star pattern with the real sky to confirm.
guideAuto.missingSensor: Automatic heading is unavailable on this device. You can still explore the sky around the target.

realSky.toggle: Show the sky as it really looks
realSky.hint: Hides stars washed out by your light pollution (Bortle) and the Moon.

sensorAuto.compassHelp: Hold your phone flat for a moment.
sensorAuto.permissionHelp: Allow once to follow your phone automatically next time.
sensorAuto.unavailable: Sensors are unavailable. You can explore the sky by touch.

guide.fovFromSettings: Based on current equipment settings; telescope field of view changes with the eyepiece.
guide.fovExampleHelp: These are starter fields of view. Enter your equipment specifications to match your view.

journey.badgeEvidence: Calculated from your saved observations and learning. Repeated objects, nights and stages count once.
